rows.name: TRON_PERFETTO_CONFIG

cells.Values and default: Path of a Perfetto config file in protobuf text format. A path that starts with `/` is used as written. Any other path is relative to the repository root. Unset: `tronperf` uses `perfetto/runtron.cfg` as the base config.
cells.Effect: `tronperf` (the Perfetto launcher for `runtron`) uses the file as its base config. `perfetto/generate-config` then changes that config with the command-line options of `tronperf`. The option `--perfetto-config` overrides it. `perfetto/wrapper` does not read it. A file that `generate-config` cannot read or parse stops `tronperf` with exit status 2.

rows.name: TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT

cells.Values and default: Whole seconds from `1` to `30`, as 1 or 2 decimal digits. `08` means 8 seconds. Any other text stops the launcher with exit status 2. Unset: 30 seconds.
cells.Effect: Sets the longest time that `tronperf` and `wrapper` (the Perfetto launchers) wait for each readiness signal. The signals come from `traced`, from `traced_probes` and from the `perfetto` client. The limit applies to each wait separately. When a wait reaches the limit, the launcher prints an error and exits with a non-zero status. The error message for a rejected value names the variable and the accepted range.

rows.name: TRON_PERFETTO_SCHEMA_DIR

cells.Set by: The Nix dev shell and the `nix run` apps `tronperf`, `wrapper`.
cells.Values and default: Path of a directory that holds the generated Python module `perfetto_config_pb2` and the file `perfetto_schema_release.txt`. Unset: `generate-config` does not change the Python module search path. It imports `perfetto_config_pb2` from the existing path.

rows.name: TRON_RUNTRON

rows.name: TRON_TP_ADDR

cells.Values and default: `HOST:PORT` of a running `trace_processor_shell --httpd` server, for example `127.0.0.1:9001`. The text is passed unchanged to the Perfetto Python package. Unset: no default address. Without a trace path and without `--addr`, the script prints an error and exits with status 2.
cells.Effect: When the command line has no trace path and no `--addr` option, the script connects to the trace processor server at that address. The server is `trace_processor_shell`, the Perfetto program that runs SQL queries on a trace. The script then loads no trace file. It does not use `--bin-path` or `TRON_TP_BIN`. The option `--addr` overrides the variable. With a trace path, the script loads the trace itself and ignores the variable.

rows.name: EXPORT_DIR

cells.Values and default: Path of a directory. A relative path starts at the working directory of the script. Unset: `exports` under the working directory.

unresolved: CABAL_INSTALL - The row says that CMake searches the name `cabal` before the value of the variable. This follows from how CMake handles `ENV CABAL_INSTALL` after `NAMES` in find_program (ingest/CMakeLists.txt:260): CMake puts the value in the argument list at that place, so it becomes one more name. The checkout does not show this CMake behavior, and the CMake manual describes `ENV` only after HINTS and PATHS. A configure run with `cmake --debug-find-variable=CABAL_EXECUTABLE` and CABAL_INSTALL set to a second cabal would settle it.
